setup_phase_untimed.counts_lineage: counts_calibration.json produced by the v2 setup phase (profiling boot under --deepep-mode normal + CALIBRATION-request pass + dump_counts.py); sha-locked here and re-verified by the v3 driver before phase 1
setup_phase_untimed.npz_conversion: counts_calibration.json {counts: 94x128} -> counts_calibration.npz {P: int64 94x128} (pure format conversion, deterministic)
setup_phase_untimed.map_generation: solve_ilp.py (MoETuner lineage, sha-locked) per layer: ILP balanced clustering (G=8 clusters x K=16 experts, minimize sum |T_c - T_bar|, time-limit 30s, mip-gap 0.005) + greedy cluster->GPU assignment + per-cluster descending-load slot fill -> frozen_map_ilp.json + meta sidecar + solve log
setup_phase_untimed.boot_validation: pre-freeze validation on CALIBRATION data only: full boot with the v3 frozen-arm launcher (warmup + cuda graph enabled, i.e. the exact measured configuration) followed by a 500-request calibration-subset bench at concurrency 256; logs and bench json sha-locked in setup_artifacts; no evaluation request served, no measured statistic produced
setup_phase_untimed.no_timing_use: setup uses no performance measurement to select anything; the map is a deterministic function of the calibration counts given the frozen solver settings
setup_phase_untimed.no_evaluation_leakage: the evaluation requests are never served before or during setup; the static map cannot encode evaluation-specific hindsight
setup_phase_untimed.attempt1_note: the first solve run completed all 94 layers (mean_imbalance 1.000, 2822.0s) but crashed in the output writer on a relative --out path and was lost; the identical settings were re-run with an absolute path (setup tooling failure, not a measured start; crash log retained and sha-locked)

metrics.primary: total_time_s per start (fixed 7963-request evaluation workload at concurrency 256 -> full-service wall time; lower is better)
metrics.source: run_grid_bench.py output json (single-machine client perf_counter; no cross-device timestamp subtraction)

statistics.design: 3 independent server starts per arm; every start enters its arm mean; no best-start or repeat selection
statistics.test: Welch two-sample t on per-start total_time_s (unequal variance), 95% CI, scipy.stats
statistics.verdict_language: frozen trichotomy: CI excludes zero -> directional effect; CI crosses zero -> 'compatible with zero' (never 'equivalence', never 'no effect proven'); negative point estimates preserved exactly as measured
statistics.validity_gate: a start is valid iff boot ok, no Traceback in server log, bench rc=0, ok==7963, errors==0; invalid starts retained with status, never retried under this frozen campaign; if an arm has <2 valid starts its contrasts are reported blocked

online_net_overhead.extraction: from arm-online server logs only: (a) sum of '(X ms)' over all '[PB-OEPLB] K swap(s) done' lines and final cumulative 'total=N' swap count; (b) last '[PB-OEPLB-PROF] window#' line cumulative record/allreduce/planbuild/finalize ms and avg_record_us; (c) '[PB-OEPLB] swap budget exhausted' line spent/elapsed if present; (d) '[PB-OEPLB-TIMING]' async_swapper lines if present; (e) window decision counts (executed/skipped/deferred/below_min_prefill) from '[PB-OEPLB] window#' lines
online_net_overhead.reporting: overhead_fraction = cumulative_swap_wall_s / mean arm-online total_time_s; reported as a mechanism decomposition alongside (NEVER subtracted from) the measured online-identity and online-frozen contrasts, because arm contrasts are already global completion-time measurements
online_net_overhead.caveat_frozen: async swapper overlaps migration with serving, so swap wall time is not purely additive latency; the fraction is an upper-bound wall-share, stated as such

controller_version_decision.decision: run the deployed site-packages version UNCHANGED: preserves lineage with prior H20 driver35/38/39 results and avoids mutating the environment inside a frozen campaign
diff_scope: repo-only: adaptive-window shrink clamp new_window=min(W,max(floor,W//2)) vs deployed max(floor,W//2)
controller_version_decision.equivalence_argument: Under the frozen online flags (sync_window=16, window_floor=8) the invariant W>=floor holds at all times (init 16>=8; shrink maps W->max(floor,W//2)>=floor; grow maps W->min(128,2W)). For any W>=floor: max(floor,W//2) <= max(W,W//2) = W, hence the deployed shrink is non-expanding and min(W,max(floor,W//2)) = max(floor,W//2). The two controller versions are therefore functionally identical on this campaign's flag set; the repo clamp differs only when floor>W (the GB200 repro case), unreachable here. The ratio-jump shrink path (max(8,W//2)) is byte-identical in both versions.

scope_note: this is the server-side full-service validation; the layer-replay crosstab (h20-placement-crosstab-v1) complements but cannot replace it
interpretation_rules: arm contrasts are whole-service effects under one fixed evaluation workload; they do not isolate MoE-layer placement effects
the frozen static arm is calibration-derived: it is a deployable-style static reference, not a hindsight optimum of the evaluation traffic
the online arm carries decision+swap overhead that the frozen arm does not; the overhead decomposition explains mechanism, it never rewrites the measured contrast
with n=3 starts per arm, CIs are wide by construction; a CI crossing zero means 'compatible with zero' at this sample size
negative effects are preserved exactly; no sign is flipped or discarded

the v3 frozen arm validates a calibration-derived ILP static reference; the greedy-descent map that failed to boot under v2 is an infrastructure-incompatibility casualty, not evidence about its serving performance
